newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Business deals fly as S.Korea's Kim visits Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Business deals fly as S.Korea's Kim visits Vietnam.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam hailed Vietnam on Thursday as "a land of hope and opportunity" while diplomats and businessmen from both countries shook hands over a raft of aid and commercial ventures.

"Now Vietnam is being transformed into a land of hope and opportunity and is spearheading Indochina's endeavours to attain a major take-off and achieve prosperity," Kim told the Korea-Vietnam Economic Cooperation Committee in Hanoi.

Kim, the first South Korean president to visit the communist country since diplomatic relations were established four years ago, arrived on Wednesday amid a razzle-dazzle of gaudy banners and media coverage.
Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, smiling broadly, told Kim that Vietnam was ready to open its doors further to the outside world -- and especially to South Korea.
Official media reports quoted Muoi as saying he wanted the people of the Korean peninsula to meet their wish for reunification through peaceful means.

Hanoi has strong ideological ties with communist North Korea. But links with Seoul have become no less important due to flourishing two-way trade and investment by Korean firms. Mutual animosity spawned by the Vietnam War is now all but forgotten.
Urging greater cooperation between Asian nations, Kim said Seoul would support Hanoi's bid for membership in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum and World Trade Organisation.

A senior Philippines official said on Wednesday that Southeast Asian nations were determined to bring Vietnam into APEC as soon as possible, perhaps even before the 18-nation group's summit in Manila next week.
Underlining the commercial tilt of his visit, Kim was accompanied on his visit by 69 South Korean business executives.
"Korea will provide unsparing support to assist in the development of those industrial sectors which Vietnam wants to foster," he told the Economic cooperation Committee.
"I hope that Vietnam will act as a bridge for advances by Korean firms into the Indochina peninsula," he said.

Official media in Vietnam reported a flurry of business ventures with South Korean companies, which have now earmarked some $2.3 billion for investment in Vietnam. The Vietnam News said the Hyundai Group broke ground in Khan Hoa province for the construction of a $95 million shipyard, which is being heralded as the biggest of its kind in Southeast Asia.

It also said the South Korean giant Daewoo Corp had been chosen to upgrade a 56-km (34-mile) section of road in the north of the country, and reported the ground breaking for a joint venture to produce telecommunication exchange equipment.

In Seoul, Ssangyong Corp said it had agreed with Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Corp and Vietnam's Vinacoal to form a $400 million joint venture to build a thermoelectric power plant in the northern town of Thai Nguyen.
Kim also signed deals with Hanoi on cooperation studies for nuclear energy and setting up Vietnam's stock exchange.

Meanwhile, the Korean Green Cross Pharmaceutical Co presented Vietnam with encephalitis B vaccine for 20,000 children, and the LG Group CN welfare foundation donated $1.0 million for the construction of schools.
